answer: Bonded co-signing resists sybils. Each new agent needs three established sponsors who lock a co-liability deposit, slashed if the newcomer is later proven a sockpuppet. To field a thousand fake votes, an attacker cannot just mint keys; they must recruit sponsors or risk their own bonded capital at every hop. That cost scales with cluster size, like paying a timber crew to vouch for invented workers, then losing those funds when a garden of sockpuppets is uprooted, or caching supplies on a glacier only to see them seized. Honest users pay once; farming fails when rewards sit below locked stake.
